speed-converter.quickAnswer: Type the speed, pick the unit you have and the one you want. Conversion uses exact definitions — 1 mph = 1.609344 km/h and 1 knot = 1.852 km/h — so results are precise, not rounded guesses.
keyFacts: One kilometre per hour equals 0.27778 metres per second; one mph equals 0.44704 m/s exactly.
The knot is one nautical mile per hour: exactly 1.852 km/h, used in aviation and sailing.
The speed of light in vacuum is 299,792,458 m/s — the universal speed limit.
Speed = distance ÷ time; converting speed units is a ratio of the underlying length and time units.
Mach 1 (speed of sound) is about 1,225 km/h at sea level, varying with temperature.
howTo: Enter the speed value in the value field.
Choose the source unit from the "From" dropdown.
Choose the target unit from the "To" dropdown.
Read the converted speed instantly; use swap to reverse it.
The rate line shows exactly how many target units equal one source unit.
speed-converter.formula:
result = value × (from-unit in m/s) ÷ (to-unit in m/s)
Example: mph = (km/h) × 0.277777778 ÷ 0.44704
benefits: Covers road (km/h, mph), science (m/s), US customary (ft/s) and marine/aviation (knots).

Does not account for wind, current or relativistic effects.

faqs.q: How do I convert km/h to mph?
faqs.a: Multiply km/h by 0.621371. Example: 100 km/h × 0.621371 = 62.1371 mph.

faqs.q: What is a knot in km/h?
faqs.a: One knot equals exactly 1.852 km/h (one nautical mile per hour). So 20 knots = 37.04 km/h.
Divide by 3.6: 36 ÷ 3.6 = 10 m/s. Dividing km/h by 3.6 always gives m/s.

faqs.q: Why do the UK and US use mph?
faqs.a: Both countries kept imperial road units. Most of the rest of the world uses km/h under the metric system.
About 1,225 km/h at sea level in standard air, but it changes with air temperature and altitude.

faqs.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faqs.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser; nothing leaves your device.

mistakes: Knots are not km/h — 20 knots is 37 km/h, not 20. Using knots as km/h on a boat nearly halves your real speed.
Pace (min/km) is the reciprocal of speed — you can't convert a runner's 5:00/km pace here. Invert it to km/h first.
mph→km/h means multiply by 1.609, not divide — dividing 60 mph by 1.609 gives 37 'km/h' of pure fiction.
Feet per second looks tiny next to km/h — 100 ft/s is 109 km/h. Don't dismiss a small ft/s number as slow.
Mach 1 isn't a fixed number — ~1,225 km/h at sea level but lower up high. This converter handles fixed units, not Mach.
